author: Ray Leathern
title: LATEST outlook for March 2026 SASSA Old-Age Grants
text:
Next month’s March 2026 SASSA Old-Age Grants are the last to disbursed at the current rate. That’s because Wednesday 18 February’s 2026 Budget Speech is typically when annual SASSA grant increases are officially finalised. And those are then paid from April onwards.
Therefore, it’ll be status quo for March 2026 SASSA Old-Age Grants, paid on Tuesday 3 March 2026 . That means R2 320 will be paid to all over 60s . And over 75s will receive R2 340 , the highest grant currently paid in South Africa …
MARCH 2026 SASSA OLD-AGE GRANTS In many ways it’s been a smooth start to the year for the South African Social Security Agency . Bar a longer-than-usual five-week wait for beneficiaries in January, there’s been little issue with the agency’s service so far this year.
Now with February and March 2026 SASSA Old-Age Grants returning to a conventional four-week cycle, attention turns to potential grant increases for the year ahead . While still to be confirmed by Finance Minister Enoch Gondongwana, the signs are good for above-inflation increases this year.
INCREASED BUDGET AND SYSTEM ISSUES SOLVED Grant amounts for the month remain unchanged, with increases expected in April. Image: File When the National Treasury increased all SASSA grants across the board last year, it was with important provisos for the Department of Social Development (DSD) . Budget for social welfare would increase from R422 billion to R452 billion over two years, but the department had to solve many weaknesses with its biometric and income reviews.
In turn, the agency said it saved hundreds of millions of Rands annually by fixing vulnerabilities within the grant system . The parliament portfolio committee liked what it heard in a sitting late last year and intimated it would increase the budget yet again if the agency could keep it up.
BEYOND MARCH 2026 SASSA OLD-AGE GRANTS Therefore, after March 2026 SASSA Old-Age Grants run next month, how much are increases likely to be? Well, ironically, consumer inflation lowered significantly in South Africa in 2025 . Previously it was around 5% , but in 2025 it came in below well that at around 3.5%. Nevertheless, if April increases stick close to 5% they will look like so:
SASSA Old-Age Grants (60-74)
Current grant: R2 320 With 5% increase: R2 430 SASSA Old-Age Grants (75 and over)
Current grant: R2 340 With 5% increase: R2 450 MIXED MESSAGES FOR SASSA GRANT INCREASES Beneficiaries will hope for above-inflation increases in the coming months. Image: File Therefore, there’s something of a cruel irony at play here. Because the economy improved last year, along with inflation, SASSA grant increases for the year may have to be more conservative than previous years .
Nevertheless, one thing that won’t change beyond March 2026 SASSA Old-Age Grants is the agency’s insistence on stricter reviews . Due to improved technology, the agency can monitor your income in real time using bank records. It also cross-references all its data with other government databases like the UIF and DHA.
INCOME AND ASSET TESTS FOR MARCH 2026 SASSA OLD-AGE GRANTS Which is why, if you’re an old-age pensioner over 60 , you have to know the asset and means test inside out:
Your income must be less than R8 983 (single) or R17 980 (married) per month. The above equates to R107 800 (single) or R215 760 (married) per annum. And your cumulative assets (property) cannot be more than R1 524 600 (single) or R3 049 200 (married). THE DOCUMENTS YOU MUST SUPPLY Despite some rocky months, Minister Sisisi Tolashe appears to have righted the ship. Image: File However, it’s also critical that you bring all necessary documents when applying for March 2026 SASSA Old-Age Grants. As The South African has reported before, applicants are regularly being turned away and asked to return if they don’t have the following documents:
Official RSA identity document (ID) preferably a Smart ID Card with digital ID photo. Valid three months’ statement certified by your bank, plus copies. All documents proving your marital status, plus death certificates if necessary. Proof of residence (a utility bill with your name on it, not older than three months ). Documents proving your income and/or financial dividends (very important). Comprehensive information regarding assets/valuation of any property you own. Full declaration of any and all private pension in your name. Unemployment Insurance Fund (UIF) membership book, or discharge certificate from your previous job. A copy of your will, first and final liquidation and distribution accounts if your spouse has passed away in the last five years . APPLYING FOR MARCH 2026 SASSA OLD-AGE GRANTS As ever, getting to a SASSA office to apply for March 2026 SASSA Old-Age Grants can be difficult. Particularly if you’re old, sick or live in a rural area. There are no online application forms for Old-Age SASSA Grants . Nevertheless, SASSA does allow family members or loved ones to help with your application.
All you need to do is produce a letter from your doctor explaining why you cannot apply yourself. And all of the above documentation must be taken to a police station and certified by a commissioner of oaths. Finally, if your grant application is denied, you have 90 days to appeal the decision HERE .
CONTACT SASSA HERE Change your life and reap your due benefits if you are a pensioner over 60. Image: File Of course, SASSA is always notoriously difficult to get hold of, with terrible queues at most offices. Nevertheless, here are their contact details:
SASSA toll-free line: 0800 601 011 Head Office of SASSA: 012 400 2322 Email SASSA: grantsenquiries@sassa.gov.za The next payment date, after March 2026 SASSA Old-Age Grants, and when new increases should be confirmed is:
Tuesday 7 April 2026 (TBC) And don’t forget to take our SASSA survey HERE and stand the chance to win R2 000 .
But what do you think? Are you excited to see how much increases will be after March 2026 SASSA Old-Age Grants? Be sure to let us know how much you’d like in the comments section below. And ask us any other questions you may need help with …
